Can hybrid language‑model serving really double its throughput without adding hardware? The paper *TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer‑Wise Streaming* (arXiv 2611.26619) says yes.

TideCache delivers up to a 2.04× increase in completed agent turns, while median per‑token latency falls by 20 %‑59 % and first‑token times speed up 1.40×‑3.05× versus the prior SGLang + HiCache baseline.

The system achieves this by dynamically reallocating HBM across heterogeneous caches, pre‑fetching the next global‑attention prefix during bounded‑state computation, and scheduling requests to run either resident or streamed based on size and queue pressure.

“Transparent Cache Pool reshuffles physical pages without changing virtual addresses.”  

These gains matter because they let operators serve more users with the same expensive GPU resources, improving QPS and reducing tail latency for interactive chat and coding agents.

The evaluation was limited to two NVIDIA Grace‑based superchips (GB300 and GH200) and seven model‑platform pairings, so results may vary on other hardware.
